name: Remove, merge or source upstream
constraints: Pseudo-tool: the recommendation is to stop doing the step, merge it into a neighbour, or obtain its output from the system that already holds it.
Never recommended when the step is required by a control (diagnostic.requiredByControl).
description: Not a product. Used so that every recommendation has a toolId, including 'do not do this step'.
notes: Engine special case: capabilities are intentionally empty and operation coverage is not checked.

name: Excel formulas and functions
constraints: Recalculates only while the workbook is open; no scheduling or triggers of its own.
Worksheet size limit: 1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns.
Data must already be in the workbook (no cross-system movement).
description: Cell formulas, lookups, SUMIFS-style aggregation, text and date functions in a spreadsheet the user already has.
notes: Row limit read from the Microsoft Excel specifications page on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: availability of dynamic-array functions (FILTER, UNIQUE, XLOOKUP) per Excel version in the target org. VERIFY: whether regular-expression worksheet functions exist in the org's Excel build before relying on transform_text_pattern for regex.

name: Excel Power Query (Get and Transform)
constraints: Refresh is user-initiated or on open in desktop Excel; no unattended schedule by itself.
Web import covers pages that serve their data as HTML tables; no JavaScript rendering.
Reads data into Excel; it does not write back to source systems.
description: Import, clean, merge and reshape data from files, databases and web tables into Excel with a recorded, repeatable query.
notes: VERIFY: scheduled refresh requires a hosting service and is not part of desktop Excel. VERIFY: connector list and any licence requirement per data source. VERIFY: Mac Excel feature parity (platform list is conservative).

name: Outlook rules
constraints: Conditions are header and keyword matches (sender, recipients, subject, body words, category); it cannot extract fields from a message body.
Actions are mailbox actions (move, categorize, flag, forward, auto-reply and similar).
Some rules run only while Outlook is running (client-only).
description: Mailbox rules that sort, flag, forward or auto-reply to incoming mail.
notes: VERIFY: which actions are server-side (Exchange) versus client-only, and the rule limits, for the org's Outlook (classic, new Outlook, Outlook on the web). The Microsoft support page for this topic returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-25, so nothing here is source-confirmed. dataFlow is an ASSUMPTION: server-side rules run in the org's mail tenant.

name: Windows Task Scheduler
constraints: Runs a program on a time-based or event-based trigger (startup, logon, idle and similar).
The machine must be on (and, for interactive tasks, the user signed in).
No built-in trigger for file arrival or new mail; use polling on a schedule.
description: OS scheduler used as the trigger companion for scripts and local automations.
notes: Trigger families read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: options for running whether or not the user is signed in, and credential storage for such tasks.

name: PowerToys PowerRename
constraints: Interactive only: launched from the File Explorer context menu; no trigger and no unattended mode.
Search and replace or regular expressions (ECMAScript grammar; optional Boost) with a preview pane and undo.
Renames files and folders only.
description: Bulk rename of selected files with search/replace or regex and a live preview.
notes: Capabilities read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. Part of Microsoft PowerToys: it must be installed and the utility enabled. VERIFY: install policy and minimum Windows version in the target org.

name: Power Automate cloud flow
constraints: Reaches only systems with a connector or API; local files and desktop apps need a gateway or a desktop flow.
Limited data shaping (no group-by aggregation of its own).
Connector licence tier (standard or premium) varies by connector.
description: Hosted low-code flows with scheduled, automated and instant triggers and prebuilt connectors.
notes: VERIFY: licence tier per connector, including the HTTP and SQL Server connectors (the Microsoft Learn HTTP connector page returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-25). VERIFY: on-premises data gateway requirement for on-premises sources. VERIFY: whether the AI and Approvals actions are covered by the org's licences. dataFlow tenant is an ASSUMPTION: the flow runs in the org's Microsoft tenant, but third-party connectors send data to those services.

name: REST / HTTP API call
constraints: A technique, not a product: it needs a host (script, flow) to run.
Needs documented endpoints, an auth method that works unattended (API key, service principal, OAuth client credentials), and rate-limit handling.
description: Direct call to a documented web API from a thin client in a host tool.
notes: VERIFY: licence tier of the HTTP action when hosted in Power Automate. Data flow is that of the host; the engine takes the higher of tool and host.

name: Microsoft Graph API
constraints: Covers Microsoft 365 services (Outlook/Exchange, Calendar, Excel, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, Planner and others).
Needs an app registration and admin-consented permissions; unattended use needs application permissions.
A technique with a host, not a standalone runner.
description: Single REST endpoint for Microsoft 365 data: mail, calendar, files, Teams, Excel workbooks in OneDrive/SharePoint.
notes: Service coverage read from the Microsoft Graph overview on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: permission model and consent process for application (unattended) access in the org. VERIFY: change-notification (webhook) support before relying on it as event_trigger; it is deliberately not listed.

name: Third-party integration platform (iPaaS)
constraints: Category entry for hosted no-code integration services; data passes through the vendor's cloud.
Coverage, task limits and data residency differ by vendor.
description: Hosted no-code connector platforms that move records between SaaS tools on triggers or schedules.
notes: VERIFY per vendor: connector coverage, limits, DPA and data residency. No vendor is named on purpose; the org's approved platform should be added as an org tool.

name: PowerShell script
constraints: Runs under the org's execution policy; when none is set the effective policy on Windows clients is Restricted, and Group Policy can override it.
Execution policy is defense in depth, not a security boundary.
Needs a trigger companion (Task Scheduler) for unattended runs.
Constrained Language Mode, WDAC or AppLocker can block scripts.
description: Scripts for file work, text and data shaping, database and API calls, and Outlook/Excel automation through their object models.
notes: Execution-policy facts read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: PowerShell version available on the target machines (Windows PowerShell versus PowerShell 7). VERIFY: org script-signing and language-mode restrictions (the environment profile has fields for these).

name: Python script
constraints: Needs an interpreter and, usually, third-party libraries; each library is a supply-chain review item.
Needs a trigger companion for unattended runs.
Static-HTML scraping only; JavaScript-rendered pages need a browser tool.
description: General scripting with a large library ecosystem for data work and API calls.
notes: VERIFY: Python is not assumed to be preinstalled on managed Windows; confirm install policy and approved package sources.

name: VBA macro (Office)
constraints: Lives inside one Office file and acts on Office objects (workbook, mailbox), not on arbitrary folders; runs in a desktop Office session; macros in files from the internet are blocked by default in Office on Windows.
Unattended use depends on a signed-in desktop session; it is not a server runtime.
description: Macros that automate Excel, Word and Outlook through their object models.
notes: Macro blocking behavior read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25 (applies to Office on Windows). VERIFY: Microsoft's support position on unattended Office automation. VERIFY: signing and Trusted Location policy in the org.

name: Office Scripts (Excel)
constraints: Acts on Excel workbooks stored in OneDrive/SharePoint; unattended runs go through Power Automate.
Its own scheduling was documented as temporarily disabled; use a Power Automate flow.
description: Recorded or hand-written scripts that automate Excel workbooks in the Microsoft 365 cloud.
notes: Description read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: licence and tenant-admin enablement requirements. Unattended execution needs a Power Automate flow, which the engine does not add automatically (add it as a companion in design).

name: SQL query or stored procedure
constraints: Runs inside one database engine; moving data to other systems needs another tool.
Scheduling comes from the database's own job scheduler.
description: Set-based data selection, aggregation and validation executed where the data lives.
notes: VERIFY: scheduling mechanism and permissions for the org's database engine; SQL dialect varies by engine.

name: AutoMate (UI automation)
constraints: Windows desktop UI automation with AutomationId-based selectors; no screen coordinates and no confidence scoring; an unresolved element fails the run loudly.
Local-only and deterministic; no AI at runtime, so it cannot host an llm_node.
Needs an unlocked interactive Windows session for unattended runs.
description: Owner's WinUI 3 / C# desktop automation tool; first automation target of Coach.
notes: Per the shared contract (decision 1). ASSUMPTION: capabilities are limited to read_from_ui, write_to_ui and transfer_data through the UI. VERIFY with the AutoMate owner: file and clipboard actions, browser-hosted UI support, unattended runner model, installer prerequisites. Because browser content rarely exposes stable AutomationIds, web apps are deliberately not listed in systemKinds.

name: Power Automate for desktop
constraints: Automates legacy and modern desktop apps, web apps, Excel and folders using UI elements, images or coordinates; the engine accepts only UI-element and DOM locators and ignores image and coordinate targeting.
Unattended runs need the Power Automate Process plan and a machine with all users signed out; elevated privileges are not supported.
description: Microsoft desktop RPA tool for UI-driven automation of desktop and web applications.
notes: Unattended requirements and locator families read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: whether the app is preinstalled on the target Windows build and which sign-in account tier the org uses. dataFlow tenant is an ASSUMPTION: flows are managed through the Microsoft cloud even when they run locally.

name: Playwright browser automation
constraints: Browser-only, DOM-selector based; needs code.
Check the site's terms and robots rules before scraping (see C-LEGAL-CHECK).
Login with interactive MFA cannot run unattended.
description: Code-driven browser automation with auto-waiting and headless mode, for JavaScript-rendered sites and web apps with no API.
notes: VERIFY: currently supported languages and browser versions; confirm the org allows installing browser binaries.

name: Regex / template field extraction
constraints: Technique run inside a host tool. Works only on text that is already machine-readable (text layer, HTML, plain text) with a stable layout.
Each new layout needs a new template.
description: Fixed-layout field extraction with regular expressions or zone templates.
notes: VERIFY: that the org's Power Automate for desktop build exposes regex text parsing before using it as a host.

name: Tesseract OCR (local)
constraints: Returns text only; field extraction is a separate step.
Accuracy depends on scan quality; handwriting is unreliable.
description: Open-source OCR engine that runs locally, so document images never leave the machine.
notes: VERIFY: current version, licence and language-pack availability. Chosen as the local-only OCR option for restricted data.

name: Document extraction service (prebuilt models)
constraints: Cloud API; documents are sent to the service in the org's cloud subscription.
Prebuilt models cover common document types (for example invoices, receipts, identity documents); other layouts need a custom-trained model.
Returns per-field confidence values at run time; thresholds are workflow design parameters, not engine inputs.
description: Managed OCR and field-extraction service with prebuilt models; product name per Microsoft docs is Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools.
notes: Name and prebuilt model list (invoice, receipt, ID) read from Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-25. VERIFY: data residency options, any disconnected/container option, API version, pricing. dataFlow tenant is an ASSUMPTION about the org's own subscription. An equivalent org-approved service can be added as an org tool.

name: Trained text classifier
constraints: Needs labeled examples (the engine's minimum is per class) and a stable label set; retraining is needed when labels drift.
Produces a label from a closed set; no free-text output.
description: Supervised classifier trained on the org's own labeled examples, run locally (for example a classical model in Python).
notes: Generic entry; a managed custom-classification service is an alternative and should be added as an org tool. VERIFY: org policy on training models with business data.

name: LLM node: cloud model
constraints: Non-deterministic; every output needs a validator and a fallback (justification card).
Data leaves the org to a model provider (managed gateway or the user's own key).
Cannot run inside AutoMate (no AI at runtime): host it in a script or flow.
description: Hosted language model called from a workflow for classification, extraction from prose, summarizing and drafting.
notes: Maps to connection types managed, byok_openrouter and byok_provider. VERIFY: provider zero-retention options per route. Context limits depend on the chosen model; maxInputSize large is an ASSUMPTION.

name: LLM node: org-hosted endpoint
constraints: Non-deterministic; justification card required.
Requires an org-provisioned OpenAI-compatible endpoint (for example a private cloud deployment, gateway or vLLM server).
Cannot run inside AutoMate: host it in a script or flow.
description: Language model served from an endpoint the organization controls.
notes: Maps to connection type custom_openai_compat. dataFlow tenant and maxInputSize large are ASSUMPTIONS that depend on how the org deploys the endpoint; the policy layer should override them per endpoint.

name: LLM node: local model
constraints: Non-deterministic; justification card required.
Runs on a localhost OpenAI-compatible server; quality and context size depend on the machine and the model.
Cannot run inside AutoMate: host it in a script or flow.
description: Small or mid-size model on the user's own machine, so content never leaves the device.
notes: Maps to connection type local. ASSUMPTION: answer_over_text and judge_quality are left out and maxInputSize is medium because small local models are weaker at long-context reasoning; the capability probe and the golden-set certification should refine this per model.

name: LLM agent (bounded tool use)
constraints: Discouraged: path is chosen by the model at run time, so behaviour is not reproducible.
Requires an allowlist of tools, a step cap, a spend cap per run, supervised (attended) use, and a human checkpoint or halt as fallback.
description: Model that plans and calls an allowlisted set of tools in a loop, for tasks whose path cannot be written down.
notes: Policy keys coach.llmAgent.mode and coach.llmOverride.mode govern use. The engine never picks this rung unless the open_ended path predicate holds.

name: Approval request (flow or Teams)
constraints: A named approver decides; the run waits for the answer.
Needs an approver mapping (who approves what) and a timeout/escalation rule.
description: Structured approve/reject request sent to a named person, with an audit trail.
notes: VERIFY: which approval features the org's Microsoft 365 / Power Automate licences include.

name: Manual review queue
constraints: A person works through flagged items from a queue (list, shared mailbox or task board).
Needs an owner, a service level and a rule for what happens when the queue is not worked.
description: Queue where items that failed a validator or matched an exception wait for a person.
notes: ASSUMPTION: dataFlow local means the tool adds no processing beyond the system the org uses for the queue; if the queue lives in a cloud service, the org should model it as an org tool with the right dataFlow.

name: Manual task with checklist
constraints: A person does the step by hand from a checklist: paper, phone calls, physical handling, or work whose path cannot be written down in advance.
Not for volume: the engine allows an open-ended manual step only up to humanMaxItemsPerRun items per run (default 50, ASSUMPTION; an org can change it).
Because a person is the worker, no system kind is excluded; the step's systems are used by hand.
description: Checklist for a person-performed step. Also the manual fallback the engine returns when a rule-based step is blocked, and the home of open-ended work that is not safe or allowed for an agent.
notes: Contract v2 puts human_checkpoint before llm_agent, so a person is the default home of open-ended work and the agent is reached only where a person is forbidden or does not fit. ASSUMPTION: the volume limit that decides 'does not fit' is a placeholder constant (DEFAULT_CFG.humanMaxItemsPerRun).
